::: {.gv-hero}
# Leakage-aware evaluation in R {.unnumbered}

::: {.gv-tagline}
Three R packages that make dataset structure explicit, keep it enforced through
resampling, and hold the line through model fitting.
:::
:::

In biomedical machine learning, most inflated performance estimates do not come
from a coding mistake. They come from structure: samples that share a subject, a
batch, a study, a sequencing run, or a timepoint. A default `vfold_cv()` splits
straight through all of it, and the resulting model looks like it generalises
when it has really only memorised a neighbour.

These three packages attack that problem at three different points in the
pipeline, and they are built to hand work to each other.

::: {.gv-pipeline}


## The packages

::: {.gv-cards .column-page}

::: {.gv-card .gv-card--splitgraph}
### [splitGraph](https://selcukorkmaz.github.io/splitGraph/)

::: {.gv-card-role}
Describe the structure
:::

Represents sample provenance, repeated measures, study design, batch effects and
temporal ordering as a typed dependency graph, then turns that graph into
deterministic split constraints.

- `graph_from_metadata()` builds the graph
- `derive_split_constraints()` reads structure off it
- `as_split_spec()` emits a tool-agnostic spec (R or JSON)

::: {.gv-card-foot}
Deliberately does **not** fit models or generate resamples.
:::
:::

::: {.gv-card .gv-card--bioleak}
### [bioLeak](https://selcukorkmaz.github.io/bioLeak/)

::: {.gv-card-role}
Enforce it, then check it
:::

Leakage-resistant split policies, preprocessing re-estimated inside every fold,
and post-hoc evidence about how much apparent performance could be leakage.

- `make_split_plan()` for subject, batch, study, time and combined axes
- `fit_resample()` and `tune_resample()` with train-only preprocessing
- `audit_leakage()` for permutation gaps and association tests

::: {.gv-card-foot}
`as_rsample()` hands the folds to tidymodels.
:::
:::

::: {.gv-card .gv-card--fastml}
### [fastml](https://selcukorkmaz.github.io/fastml/)

::: {.gv-card-role}
Model without re-introducing leakage
:::

Trains, tunes and benchmarks many models through one call, with preprocessing
and fitting re-estimated within each resampling split rather than once up front.

- `fastml()` trains and compares a whole set of algorithms
- `resamples =` accepts folds built upstream
- `fastexplain()` for SHAP, LIME, ALE, ICE and surrogates

::: {.gv-card-foot}
Orchestrates tidymodels engines; it does not replace them.
:::
:::

:::

## Which one do I need?

| If you want to... | Reach for |
|---|---|
| Write down how your dataset is actually structured, and have that be checkable | `splitGraph` |
| Confirm a split honours the subject / batch / study / time axes it claims to | `splitGraph` or `bioLeak` |
| Build folds that respect those axes, and impute or scale without leaking | `bioLeak` |
| Ask how much of your AUC could be leakage or confounding | `bioLeak` |
| Train and compare many algorithms on already-safe folds | `fastml` |
| Explain a fitted model (SHAP, LIME, ALE, ICE) | `fastml` |
| Hand a split definition to a Python collaborator | `splitGraph` (JSON `split_spec`) |

: {tbl-colwidths="[78,22]"}

## Installation

``` r
install.packages(c("splitGraph", "bioLeak", "fastml"))
```

Development versions:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak(c(
  "selcukorkmaz/splitGraph",
  "selcukorkmaz/bioLeak",
  "selcukorkmaz/fastml"
))
```

::: {.gv-scope}
**Scope.** These packages reduce leakage *risk*. None of them proves the absence
of leakage or guarantees an unbiased performance estimate. What they do is make
structural assumptions explicit and testable, which is a different and more
modest claim. Each package states its own limits on its own site.
:::

## Why there is no `guardedverse` package

Suites like [fastverse](https://fastverse.org) and the tidyverse ship an umbrella
package that attaches the others. There is deliberately no such package here.

An umbrella earns its place when it does something its members cannot: resolve
conflicts, manage extensions, pin versions. A package whose only job is
`library(splitGraph); library(bioLeak); library(fastml)` would add a release
cycle, a CRAN dependency, and a reverse-dependency burden in exchange for two
saved lines.

What these three packages actually share is a *sequence* and a *vocabulary*, and
both live better in a site than in a `Depends:` field. If a genuinely shared
abstraction hardens later — the `split_spec` contract is the obvious candidate —
an umbrella package becomes worth the cost. It is not worth it yet.
